Neither idx has a required witness. test4 is that same dedicated test file.

t3 implements ReviewProgressSource, ReviewDelegateBase and the concrete DesignReviewDelegate/CodeReviewDelegate (review-measurements.ts lines 161-167 and 246-329): idx6 (shared imports plus the isNewer/isHeartbeat/progress scaffolding and its tests) and idx7 (ReviewKey/DelegateMeasurement imports, the interface and the rest of the class body) are the implementation; idx8/idx9/idx11/idx13/idx15/idx16 are the remaining class-body lines (ownerActivity, processAlive, the subclasses). idx6's witnesses [8,10,12], idx7's witnesses [9,11,13,15,16], idx9's witness [11,13,15] and idx11's witness [13] are all already members of this same set, so t3's scope is self-contained with no omitted witness. The matching tests (fakeSource double, delayed-incarnation, heartbeat-only, interrupted-until-verified, missing/closing/throwing-source, the real-ReviewWorkers non-interference test, and ownerActivity liveness) sit at lines 160-332 of review-measurements.test.ts (idx6/8/10/12/14), all carried by test2, shared with t2 since both live in the same file.

t5 binds an admitted review to a coordinator task through the daemon-internal launchReview seam. review-measurements.ts's BindReviewTaskDeps/withOwnedFence/bindReviewTask (idx27) is the core, and its required witness idx35 (reviewTerminalEvidence plus the remainder of withOwnedFence) is now included; access.ts's ProgressAccess.launchReview (idx26) is the seam it calls; review-workers.ts's bindTask dependency field, taskBinding entry field and the fire-and-forget bind-at-admission call in admit (idx30) wire it into admission; review-service.ts's bindTask plumbing through ProductionReviewDeps (idx25) and handler-runtime.ts's progressRuntime dependency threading (idx17) connect the daemon's composed runtime to that path; daemon/index.ts's bindTask construction call (idx24) is where it is instantiated. review-task-binding.test.ts (idx29,32,33) is the dedicated integration test, using the shared review-stub-worker.ts helper (idx28, whose required witness idx36 is included). Its one named test, 'the normalized projection of an unobserved review is unchanged', is review-task-signal.test.ts lines 224-249 (idx40) -- an unobserved admission (session connection) leaves no store record while an adjacent observed review is bound, and the unobserved review's progressOf projection is byte-identical before and after. LLD.md's new t5 pre-check outcome section (idx39) is exactly the design-notes update the task summary calls for, recording the launchReview seam decision into the LLD open questions. test0 (review-task-signal.test.ts) is shared with t6.

tasks.summary: t1's progressOf accessor (review-workers.ts:509-516) is a pure read-only projection: it looks up the entry, returns undefined for an unknown key, a closing entry, or an entry with no accepted progress yet, and otherwise returns a frozen structuredClone of the stored progress, satisfying the no-writes / no-sequence-advance / no-board-or-worker-interaction requirement. The dedicated test file exercises all four required behaviors: unknown key returns undefined; the clone is immutable (mutation throws, cachedProgress stays unchanged); the closing-window race is covered by aborting the owner connection and polling until cachedProgress is present while progressOf is undefined; shutdown yields undefined; and five repeated calls leave sequence, board snapshot and worker postMessage calls unchanged.

testCoverage.explanation: Inspected the full bodies of both tests in review-workers-progress-of.test.ts (lines 1-87). Test one asserts an unknown key returns undefined; after admit, admission-phase progress is visible; after acceptProgress, progressOf reflects the new sequence, phase, completed, total and observation; the returned object throws TypeError on mutation and cachedProgress is unaffected by mutating the clone; two successive progressOf calls return deep-equal but distinct objects (fresh clone per call); after owner-connection abort it polls until cachedProgress is still present while progressOf returns undefined, then after shutdown progressOf is undefined. Test two asserts five repeated progressOf calls leave cachedProgress sequence and object identity unchanged, leave the board snapshot JSON unchanged, post no message to the worker (a postMessage spy is installed for the duration of the reads), and leave updatedAt unchanged. These assertions directly cover the task's four acceptance checks. The daemon gate ran this file and recorded a pass. The stored test-case names for this task in the build record do not literally match the real test titles in the file, but the gate command runs the whole file with no name filter, so this is a labeling inaccuracy rather than a gate bypass.

advice: Optional execution: did not independently re-run the review-workers-progress-of test file; relying on the daemon gate's recorded pass plus direct inspection of the test bodies against the implementation.

Minor record hygiene: the test-case names stored for this task in the build record do not match the actual test titles in the file. Harmless since the gate runs the whole file, but worth aligning the recorded names to the real titles.
